playbook:
When told to hide, I choose a cell that balances unpredictability and proximity to where I expect others not to concentrate; I avoid always picking the exact center and I avoid repeating the same hide cell every round to reduce exploitable patterns.

When posting a station note, I publish neutral, non-accusatory phrasing that neither reveals precise intent nor invites immediate targeting (examples: "all systems nominal", "steady on station"). If I want to encourage reciprocal escort behavior, I use a slightly more inviting but still non-specific phrasing (examples: "available for close cover" or "standing by to assist") only when I am prepared to follow through.

When the standing order directs me to fire at the next live station, I generally follow it unless there is a clear strategic reason not to (Harbor rules, clear mutual cooperation opportunity elsewhere). I aim to vary my firing cells across rounds rather than repeating the same number (avoid firing 6 every round). I choose cells that are plausible given my hide history and intended unpredictability (mix center, offsets, flanks).

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, I always report that result truthfully in my public claim; I do not misreport hits or misses. I use others' claims and the hit/miss pattern to infer likely hidden positions over rounds and to detect targeted retaliation or collusion.

When considering firing on Harbor, I do not fire on Harbor unless the expected net payoff (including the guaranteed jettison penalty and political fallout) clearly outweighs costs; my default is: do not fire Harbor. If I do decide to fire Harbor, I treat it as a committed, explicit strategic move and signal that in my notes only if necessary to influence others.

When choosing an escort claim, I name another boat only if there is a plausible mutual benefit or reasonable evidence the other will reciprocate. I do not make unilateral escort claims for appearance. If I want to try to secure a mutual escort, I coordinate via an inviting but non-specific note that signals willingness to reciprocate; if that yields no reciprocal signal in the next round or two, I revert to claiming none.

When posting notes to induce reciprocal escort claims, I avoid explicitly naming a partner in a public note; instead I invite mutual recognition with phrasing that indicates willingness to coordinate. If I see identical neutral notes from others repeatedly, I interpret that as possible tacit collusion and either (a) try to break the symmetry by offering reciprocal support to one specific boat with a follow-up inviting note, or (b) avoid committing and play defensively.

When the picket order cycles, I maintain consistent compliance to avoid becoming an obvious target for retaliation; I deviate from the order only with a clear, communicated strategy or if following the order would cause unacceptable loss (e.g., firing at Harbor without justification).

When my shot history shows repeated misses versus a particular opponent, I vary firing cells and consider shifting between conservative and probing shots to test hidden positions rather than persisting with one unsuccessful number. Use misses to map the nine-cell line over rounds and exploit any emerging pattern.

When my score is leading, I play conservatively: avoid risky attacks that could provoke multiple boats or attract collective retaliation; prefer neutral notes and claiming none for escort unless mutual payoffs are likely. When behind and needing points, prioritize accurate, pattern-exploiting shots against opponents who show exposure and actively seek mutual escort claims by signaling cooperation in notes.

When tempted to claim an escort for appearance only, I do not do it—false unilateral claims waste opportunities and can reveal nothing. I only make escort claims when I either have reciprocation or am intentionally seeding a two-step coordination attempt (signal in note this round, claim next round if reciprocated).

When a round's public notes show opponents repeating identical notes or positions, I consider two responses: exploit predictability by varying my hides and fires, or attempt to break/invite cooperation by posting a distinct but non-aggressive note that signals willingness to reciprocate. Choose the response that best fits my score situation and risk tolerance.

I use public claims (hits/misses) from others to update my model of their hide-and-fire strategies and to detect possible collusion (pairs consistently naming each other for escorts or making coordinated notes). If two boats name each other for escort, I treat that as likely real and avoid competing for the same mutual partnership unless I can outbid with clear reciprocation.

I keep a simple tempo: vary hide positions, vary firing cells, post neutral notes by default, escalate invitation for escort only when I will reciprocate, never lie about shot results, avoid Harbor unless strategically justified, and prioritize reciprocal escort gains over unilateral, symbolic claims.

If I see a clear opportunity to secure the 5+5 escort payoff (mutual naming) I will actively signal and then claim reciprocally; if the opportunity fails to materialize, I stop signaling and revert to defense.

When asked to hide, place me centrally for the first round (cell 4–6) to maximize coverage.
When asked to hide on later rounds, move to a different cell than my previous hide; do not repeat the same cell twice in a row.
When given a standing firing order, follow it unless I have a clear, signaled reason to deviate (explicit ally coordination for escort payoff or a tactical reason); default is to fire at the next live station in the order Echo→Foxtrot→Gamma→Echo.
When choosing a firing coordinate, randomize among a small set (e.g., three nearby cells) rather than using the identical cell every round; actively rotate choices so I do not use the same fire cell consecutively.
When the office privately reports my shot result, copy it exactly in my public claim (I must always report the private truth).
When I get a hit, claim it immediately and note it if useful to justify or facilitate coordination with the shooter/target in my station notes.
When I get a miss, claim it honestly; do not invent hits (claims are validated).
When posting a station note, use brief, unambiguous signals that can be reciprocated by allies for coordination (e.g., “steady on station,” “holding,” or a short agreed phrase). Reciprocate neutral notes when they serve to maintain coordination; avoid gratuitous repetition of the same phrasing if I want to signal a change.
When seeking escort points, coordinate an explicit two-way commitment via notes: name a preferred partner in a note when safe, then on escort stage name that partner only if they have signaled reciprocal intent.
When unable to coordinate a reciprocal escort, claim none rather than naming someone who didn’t reciprocate.
When Harbor is present, do not fire at Harbor unless there is a decisive reason to accept the jettison penalty; default: avoid attacking Harbor.
When my score or allies’ scores lag and mutual escorts are feasible, prioritize securing mutual escorts over chasing uncertain hits—mutual escort yields steady +5 each and is lower variance.
When uncertain about allies’ intentions, use neutral notes (“maintaining station,” “steady”) rather than misleading or provocative language.
When I notice my behavior is predictable (same hide cells, same fire cells, same notes), deliberately vary one axis (hide, fire, or note) next turn to break patterns; in practice prioritize varying fire cells first, then hide position, then note phrasing.
When a tactical deviation is proposed by an ally (e.g., agreeing to mutually escort or to alternate targets), accept only if I can obtain clear reciprocal signaling; otherwise stick to default honest play.
Keep an internal record of recent hits/misses on each opponent and avoid repeatedly firing the same coordinate at a target that has repeatedly missed; prefer distributing shots across my small set to probe possible target locations.
If I score an early hit on an opponent, treat that opponent as a candidate for reciprocal cooperation (use notes to suggest pairing) but do not rely on implied loyalty without explicit escort signals.
If I must repeat a strategic pattern for clarity (e.g., to signal intent), do so at most two rounds before deliberately altering it to avoid being exploited.
When forced to choose between a small probability of a hit and securing a guaranteed escort payoff from a reciprocal partner, prefer the guaranteed escort if it can be reliably obtained by signaling.
When the picket contains more than three live boats or Harbor is behaving aggressively, reassess the balance of hunting versus escorting and favor low-variance escort coordination unless hunting produces clear, repeatable returns.

2.text:
When asked to pick a hide cell, I vary deliberately: favor midline cells (4–6) for balance but switch to less-used cells (1–3 or 7–9) on the next opportunity so my sequence is not predictable. I avoid repeating the same hide two rounds in a row and prefer an off-center choice after a round where I was targeted.

When asked for a station note, I default to mirroring the formation tone (e.g., "steady on station") to avoid early commitments. If I want to open for an alliance I use a short, noncommittal, invitation-style phrase (e.g., "steady — watch your six") that signals willingness without revealing my hide. I do not gloat or broadcast hit details in notes.

When the standing order names a target, I follow it by default. I will consider deviating only if there is a clear, enforceable alliance opportunity (mutual escort promise backed by prior reciprocal behavior) or a tactical reason (e.g., a boat is demonstrably carrying the payroll and the jettison calculus favors striking). Deviations must be based on observable reciprocation or a clear points advantage, not on speculation.

When choosing a shot coordinate, I avoid firing the same number repeatedly. I alternate between central and edge choices within a loose pseudo-random scheme (e.g., center one round, flank the next, then an off-center mid). I avoid clustering all shots on one cell across rounds. If I have intelligence that a given cell is productive, I may bias toward it but still intersperse unpredictability.

When the office privately tells me hit or miss, I file the claim that matches the true result. Truthful claims preserve credibility for negotiating escorts and make reciprocity signals interpretable.

When I get a hit on another boat, I keep the information private for tactical planning. I do not change public notes to gloat; instead I use the hit to reassess whether to pursue escort agreements, retaliatory targeting, or to alter hide/shot patterns.

When thinking about escort claims, I attempt mutual escorts only when reciprocity is likely and enforceable — for example, after at least one round of reciprocal escort gestures or consistent supportive behavior (not just a single note). I will explicitly refrain from claiming an escort I did not receive unless I have arranged a credible swap. If mutual escort seems unlikely, I claim "none".

When offered or contemplating collusion to swap escorts for points, I require signs of trust before committing: prior truthful claims, repeated non-aggression, or a two-step signaling sequence (neutral note then small supportive action). I will not trade escorts based solely on a single benign note.

When Harbor is in play, I treat its warning as meaningful deterrence. I will not fire on Harbor unless the immediate +3 payoff and tactical position (e.g., can secure mutual escorts or eliminate a strong rival) clearly outweigh predicted retaliation and loss of future alliance potential.

When my shot result history shows no useful pattern, I stick to randomized hides and varied shot choices and keep notes bland. Avoid flashy or inflammatory claims that draw coordinated retaliation.

When I want to cultivate an ally for mutual escorts, I establish credibility first: keep notes neutral but consistent, make truthful claims, and demonstrate non-aggression for a couple rounds before proposing mutual salvage. Use small, observable supportive actions (e.g., not targeting them when standing order would otherwise) to build trust.

When lacking reliable intel or reciprocation, I claim "none" for salvage and avoid pursuing forced alliances that risk points or expose pattern. Prioritize preserving my own scoring opportunities over speculative promises.

Behavioral operational rules I will follow next time:
- Never fire the same coordinate more than twice in a row; if I have used the same coordinate twice, change to a different parity (odd/even) and different region (center/edge).
- Do not escort unless I have received at least one explicit reciprocating escort in a prior round or two credible supportive signals.
- Use notes to invite reciprocity only when I can follow through the next round; otherwise keep notes strictly neutral.
- Only break the standing-order target if I can document a reciprocal agreement or a clear points advantage from diverging.
- Continue truthful claims for private shot results to preserve negotiation leverage and clarity.

I retain the overall conservative posture: varied hides, follow-standing-order by default, truthful claims, escort only when enforceably reciprocal, and avoid firing on Harbor unless the calculus is decisive.
